name: Pine64 (Pine Store Limited)
subcategory: community-oriented ARM/RISC-V single-board computers, laptops, phones and wearables
origin_detail: Founded in October 2015 in Fremont, California as Pine Microsystems Inc. by TL Lim (CEO, earlier behind PopBox and Popcorn Hour media players) and Johnson Jeng; launched with a December 2015 Kickstarter for the Pine A64 board that raised over $1.7M. Pine Store Limited was incorporated in Hong Kong in December 2019 and Pine Microsystems Inc. was dissolved in January 2020.
openness_notes: Hardware column. Pine64 sells low-cost hardware and relies on community-run, open-source software (mainline Linux and many PinePhone OS projects; InfiniTime on the PineTime; IronOS on the Pinecil), and describes letting 'FOSS principles guide our business'. For hardware it publishes schematic PDFs, component placement drawings, component lists and certification documents (e.g. PinePhone mainboard v1.1-v1.2b), but no PCB/Gerber layouts, and no open hardware licence is stated (only '(c) 2026 PINE64'). In July 2026 it released the full 3D (STEP) file of the PinePhone and PinePhone Pro case assembly to enable self-repair and custom parts; the post states no licence. Open software plus viewable but unlicensed, incomplete hardware documentation = level 2. Level at the first product (2016) was not verified.

license_history.license: Schematic PDFs and placement drawings published without an open hardware licence (PinePhone v1.1 'Braveheart' onward)
license_history.note: Year is the PinePhone Braveheart release (Feb 2020); publication date of the PDFs not verified. Footer copyright notice only; no CERN-OHL/CC licence found.

relicensing_events.outcome_note: No licence stated in the release post; described as a possible 'final hurrah' for this PinePhone generation.

risk_events: 2016: Pine A64 Kickstarter deliveries overshadowed by delays and shipping problems
2019-2020: corporate base moved from Fremont, California (Pine Microsystems Inc., dissolved Jan 2020) to Hong Kong (Pine Store Ltd); orders governed by Malaysian law as of late 2020
Ongoing: software support depends on volunteer community projects rather than the company
2026: PineTime revision needed to replace an end-of-life display part

2025-08: PinePhone Pro discontinued because it 'didn't sell well enough to keep production going'; spare parts promised for up to two years, original PinePhone to stay in production about two more years
2026-05: disclosed a Desktop PinePower V2 bug where some USB-C ports can report 0V with a device attached
2026-07: founder says a PinePhone 2 is not planned for now (large financial risk, no suitable SoC); focus has shifted to RISC-V boards and AI work
robustness: Hardware is made and sold only by Pine64, but most software is community-maintained open source that would outlive the company, and published schematics help repair and porting. Small, low-margin business with no disclosed outside investment; still shipping new products in 2026 (PineVoice speaker, PineTime Pro samples).
physical_science_relevance: Low-cost ARM and RISC-V boards (Star64, Ox64) and the open-firmware Pinecil soldering iron are usable in lab automation, teaching and instrument prototyping.
openness_effect_assessment: Pine64 outsourced most software development to an open-source community (17 OS releases for the PinePhone per Wikipedia), which let a small company sell Linux phones, laptops and watches it could not have supported alone. Its hardware openness is partial (schematic PDFs, no layouts, no open licence), and the dependence on volunteers is also its main weakness. It remains operating and launching products in 2026 on Kickstarter-scale initial funding. It discontinued the PinePhone Pro in August 2025 for weak sales and in July 2026 ruled out a PinePhone 2 for now, citing financial risk.
key_takeaway: Pine64 is the 'community supplies the software, company supplies cheap hardware' model: openness lives mostly in community-maintained software, while hardware is documented (schematics, now 3D files) but not openly licensed. Founded in California and moved to Hong Kong in 2019-2020, it has survived a decade on crowdfunding and sales rather than VC, at small scale.

contradicted.evidence: PINE64 has so far raised over $1.4 million in its Kickstarter campaign for their tiny, yet versatile, $15 computer.
contradicted.note: This article, dated 2016-01-21, is the reference Wikipedia cites for '$1.7 million in December 2015'. It shows the campaign still raising money in late January 2016, so a $1.7M total cannot be as of Dec 2015 (Dec 2015 is when the campaign started). Not applied: TechCrunch is third-party journalism (already in the file's sources), and the close date was not found.

unconfirmed.reason: Only Wikipedia's infobox gives October 2015, and it is uncited there. pine64.org/about/ is a 404, the pine64.org homepage, documentation index and Pine_A64 documentation page give no founding or Kickstarter date, and the pine64.com store shows only 'Pine Store ltd. Copyright 2022'. The California SOS filings Wikipedia cites sit on a retired host (businesssearch.sos.ca.gov does not resolve), and the tool cannot fetch the Internet Archive copy. TechCrunch (2016-01-21) names co-founder Johnson Jeng but gives no founding date.

Only Wikipedia states 'over US$1.7 million'. The reference it cites (TechCrunch, 2016-01-21, in the file's sources) gives only an interim 'so far raised over $1.4 million', which neither confirms nor contradicts a final $1.7M. The Kickstarter campaign page returned 403.
Only Pine64's own cited post and homepage state the July 2026 3D-file release. The PinePhone 'Schematics and certifications' page lists no 3D/STEP files and no licence (footer '© 2026 PINE64' only).

verification_pass2.note: The source chain is weaker than it looks. Wikipedia's founding month (Oct 2015) and its co-founder are uncited, and the TechCrunch reference cited for '$1.7M in December 2015' actually says '$1.4 million so far' on 2016-01-21. The TechCrunch source entry in the file says 'not fetched'; it was fetched in this pass. origin_detail's Hong Kong entity is confirmed by a government registry: Hong Kong Companies Registry report RNC063 (02-08 Dec 2019) lists 'PINE STORE LIMITED 2899554 05-12-2019', i.e. incorporated 5 Dec 2019. pine64.com's footer reads 'Pine Store ltd. Copyright 2022'.
